Description: Bronze coins of Herod Antipas, tetrarch of Galilee and Peraea (4 BC-AD 39), struck at the Tiberias mint in four denominations (eight units to a denarius). The first series (year 24 = AD 20/21) names the city 'Tiberias' in Greek within a wreath on one side with a reed on the other — the first Jewish coinage to name a city. Middle series (years 33, 34, 37 = AD 29/30, 30/31, 33/34) pair 'Tiberias' in a wreath with a palm branch inscribed 'Herod the Tetrarch'; the final series is year 43 (AD 39). No series carries portraits or figural images.
Interpretations: The coins name Herod the Tetrarch and his capital Tiberias, and their avoidance of graven images — unusual for a ruler of his time — shows deference to the Jewish ban on images, matching the picture of a ruler balancing Jewish and Roman worlds. Antipas issued only five series in 43 years, and none before his 24th regnal year, suggesting a light footprint in Galilee.
BiblicalSignificance: Mark 6 names 'king Herod' hearing of Jesus and recalls his execution of John the Baptist; these are the coins of that tetrarch, struck at Tiberias in the very years of John's death and Jesus' ministry.
